name: SUNDAY Pangola Falls, Double Creek Falls, and Double Gorge
description:
Date: Sunday, 27th November 2022

Who is Leading - Ian Wallace
Max group size - 15 people.
Grade - Easy - a bit of trail and rock hoping. This walk is for absolute beginners. 
Distance: ~3kms return
Duration:  Quarter-day walk; ~2-3 hours (not including vehicle travel there and back)

Description 
Beginning on private property, we will walk on a rough track to the creek and then rock hop upstream to Pangola Falls, and then upstream furhur to Double Creek Falls and Double Gorge.
If it rains or the rocks are wet, we will only go to the first waterfall (on track). 

Since we are accessing this place via private property, we will either help the owner with a simple task prior or post walk for 30 mintues. 

What to expect:
-Creek crossings and rock hopping
-The terrain is undulating with some steep sections


Meeting Point - 
Meeting details will be sent closer to the date.
RSVP link below

What to bring:
-Water: 1-2 litres recommended
-Sunscreen & hat, Sunsafe clothing 
-Insect repellent
-Shoes appropriate for walking on rocky, uneven surfaces. Acceptance that you may be walking in wet shoes as we will be crossing some creeks. 
-Car clothes for the trip home, and maybe thongs for after the walk
-Swimming togs & towel if planning to swim
-Trail snacks, morning tea
-Camera
-First-aid kit and snake bite bandage

Check out this blog for more info on the area:
https://wanderstories.space/sharp-elliot-and-double-creek/

🛑🛑
Please note - this event is FREE for TBWC members
For Visitors of the TBWC - there is a fee of $5
To RSVP - Because this is a TBWC event, RSVP is a bit different - please do so via this form below:

If you RSVP to an event and can't make it, please email info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com to let them know with as much notice as possible. It is just plain courtesy, so that people on the waitlist can take your spot.

name: Paluma - Diorite Falls
description:
Date: Sunday, 20th November 2022

Who is Leading - Cherry Judge

Rate - Medium - on trial mostly, with a few creek crossings. This is not a walk for absolute beginners. 
Consider the distance involved in your decision making. The pace will be moderate and steady, so we can cover the distance within the designated time-frame and enjoy our stops at the points of interest mentioned above.


Description 
Beginning at the Paluma Dam campground, we’ll head north along the dam wall and then through the rainforest to the Diorite Falls. We’ll spend some time there, so there will be an opportunity for a swim and a look around – I reckon it should be looking pretty good after recent rainfall. After that we’ll take a different trail back to the Paluma Dam campground, basically we'll be doing an extended clockwise circuit around the dam.

What to expect:
-Creek crossings and rock hopping
-The terrain is undulating with some steep sections
-We make a gradual descent to Diorite Falls, and the ascent on the return journey involves a lot of uphill including one section which is around 1km of constant uphill.

Approximate:
-Distance: 18-20kms
-Duration: 6-7 hours including stops & breaks
Meeting Point - 
The dirt carpark next to Ampol Yabulu (Ingham direction) at 6:00am – From here we’ll carpool to the start point of the hike at the Paluma Dam.
Or Paluma Dam at 7:15 ish


What to bring:
-Water: 3-4 litres recommended
-Sterilisation tablets if you plan to refill your water supply from creeks
-Electrolytes if needed
-Sunscreen & hat, Sunsafe clothing 
-Insect repellent
-Shoes appropriate for walking on rocky, uneven surfaces. Acceptance that you will be walking in wet shoes as we will be crossing some creeks. 
-Dry clothes and maybe thongs for after the walk
-Swimming togs & towel if planning to swim
-Trail snacks, morning tea and lunch
-Salt for leeches
-Rain poncho
-Camera
-First-aid kit and snake bite bandage
-Secateurs

Check out this blog for more info on the area:
https://wanderstories.space/diorite-falls/

For further information and extensive trail maps around Paluma in general, check out: http://paluma.org/

name: Bluegum Ck + Triple Falls
description:
Who is leading - Ian Wallace

About the walk:
We will walk the Bluegum Circuit in a clockwise direction, starting along the H-Track.

Along the track we will be taking a detour to visit Triple Falls. Then we continue along the track till we come to a lagoon [on Star River] and then continue along to Miner Creek Falls. From here we start our ascent out of the valley back up to Paluma Village.

What to expect:
- Steep and uneven sections with ropes in place to assist in a couple of places
-Rock hopping & Scrambling
-Downstream from the lagoon, there is no well-defined track

What to bring:
-Water: 3-4 litres
-Sterilisation tablets if you’re planning to refill your water from creeks
-Electrolytes if needed
-Sunscreen & hat
-Insect repellent
-Shoes appropriate for walking on rocky, uneven surfaces
-Dry clothes and maybe thongs for after the walk
-Swimming togs & towel if planning to swim
-Trail snacks, morning tea and lunch
-Salt for leeches
-Rain poncho
-Camera
-First-aid kit and snake bite bandage

For more information on the trail and general area, check out the following links:
https://wanderstories.space/bluegum-creek-circuit/
http://paluma.org/

MEETING POINT: 6:00 am at Caltex Yabulu Service station, 25km north of Townsville, in the dirt carpark.

RSVP
This event is free for TBWC members
For visitors, it is $5 for insurance cover.
Must be 18+years to attend.

Please RSVP at this link - https://forms.gle/jsMKXeDvWfT2vkZj8
